# Cap Blanc Rock Shelter

Cap Blanc (Abri du Cap Blanc) is one of the most important Upper Paleolithic archaeological sites in France, renowned for its exceptional prehistoric sculptured frieze.

## Location
Located in the Dordogne region of southwestern France, near the commune of Marquay, about 7 km from Les Eyzies-de-Tayac, in the Vézère Valley.

## Dating
The site dates to the **Magdalenian period** (approximately 15,000-13,000 years ago), during the Upper Paleolithic.

## The Sculptured Frieze

The most remarkable feature is a **monumental bas-relief sculpture** carved directly into the limestone rock shelter wall:

- **Approximately 13 meters long**
- Features primarily **horses** - at least 5-6 horses are clearly identifiable
- Also includes depictions of **bison** and possibly other animals
- The sculptures are life-sized or near life-sized
- Carved in high and low relief, some figures are quite three-dimensional
- Represents one of the finest examples of Paleolithic sculptural art

## Discovery
- Discovered in **1909** by French archaeologist **Dr. J. G. Lalanne**
- The site was inhabited and used as a living space during the Magdalenian

## The Cap Blanc Burial
A significant **human burial** was discovered at the site:
- Originally thought to be a woman (called the "Dame de Cap Blanc")
- More recent analysis suggests it may have been a young man
- Found in close association with the sculptures
- One of the few Magdalenian burials found in direct association with parietal art

## Significance
- One of the best-preserved examples of Paleolithic rock sculpture
- Demonstrates advanced artistic and technical skills
- Part of the UNESCO World Heritage site "Prehistoric Sites and Decorated Caves of the Vézère Valley" (inscribed in 1979)
- Provides insights into Magdalenian culture and artistic expression

## Current Status
- The site is protected and can be visited by the public
- Managed as a museum site
- Viewing is carefully controlled to preserve the delicate sculptures

The Cap Blanc frieze represents a rare example of monumental Paleolithic sculpture and stands as a testament to the artistic sophistication of Ice Age peoples.
